items.answer: Extended reality (XR) is an umbrella term, not a specific technology, that covers all present or future immersive technologies, such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and mixed reality (MR).

items.prompt: What is non-immersive virtual reality system?
items.answer: A non-immersive virtual reality system is a limited class of computer application that provides a computer-generated environment in which a user controls characters or activities while retaining control of the physical environment. The user is psychologically engaged and remains physically attached to the real world, while the virtual environment does not directly interact with the user.

items.prompt: What is semi-immersive virtual reality system?
items.answer: Semi-immersive virtual reality system is a type of virtual reality system, positioned between non-immersive and fully immersive systems, that gives the user a partial immersive experience by blocking some but not all senses while leaving the user free to sense the real world.

items.prompt: What is fully immersive virtual reality system?
items.answer: Fully immersive virtual reality system is a virtual reality system that completely blocks the user's ability to sense the real world by blocking all senses, so the user senses only the virtual world and feels physically present in it.

Augmented reality (AR) is an enhanced version of reality created by technology, in which computer-generated digital content is overlaid on the real world in real time and registered in 3D, so the user perceives and interacts with the enhanced environment.

An immersive experience is a perceived experience through sensory organs that appears real, because a person cannot distinguish the experienced environment from their real environment and perceives it as that real environment.

questions.question: Which statement best captures how augmented reality differs from virtual reality?
options: Augmenting real-world content with digital content
Creating a fully immersive experience with digital content
Replacing real-world content with digital content
Presenting a simulated environment with digital content
questions.explanation: Augmented reality adds digital content to the real world rather than replacing it or requiring a fully immersive experience.

questions.question: What can augmented reality help an archaeologist do?
options: Hide existing structures
Measure existing structures
Replace lost structures
Reconstruct lost structures
questions.explanation: In archaeology, augmented reality can display things not visible to the naked eye and reconstruct lost structures, not replace, hide, or simply measure them.

questions.question: What can augmented reality allow a person to do while repairing or troubleshooting an industrial component?
options: Automate things
Hide things
Replace things
See things
questions.explanation: In industrial manufacturing, augmented reality can let a person see things during repair or troubleshooting; it is not described as replacing, hiding, or automating things.

questions.question: The presence of many applications in e-commerce is one motivation for the metaverse concept in which technology?
options: Extended reality
Mixed reality
Virtual reality
Augmented reality
questions.explanation: Many augmented reality applications in commerce, particularly e-commerce, are one motivation for the metaverse concept, not virtual, mixed, or extended reality generally

data.text: XR has broad application potential across many fields, but AR is the form that adds digital content to the real world rather than requiring immersion. This augmentation appears in domains such as archaeology, manufacturing, and commerce, where AR can reveal hidden details or help with repair. The presence of many AR applications in commerce, especially e-commerce, is one motivation for the metaverse concept.
points: Extended reality (XR) can be applied in games, healthcare, engineering, live events, video entertainment, real estate, retail, and military.
Augmented reality (AR) does not require an immersive experience, unlike virtual reality (VR), but augments real-world content with digital content.
AR applications include archaeology, architecture, industrial manufacturing, commerce especially e-commerce, gaming, and medical domains.
AR can reveal hidden archaeological details, reconstruct lost structures, and help with industrial repair or troubleshooting.
The presence of many AR applications in commerce, especially e-commerce, is one motivation for the metaverse concept.

questions.question: Why are beacons placed throughout a large airport terminal in an AR passenger app?
options: To locate the passenger and show direction to a desired terminal
To display virtual shop tours throughout the large terminal
To estimate the walking distance between every gate inside the terminal
To show live flight updates near the main terminal
questions.explanation: The beacons let the app determine where the passenger is and direct them toward a desired terminal. They are not described as providing shop tours, walking distances, or live flight updates.

questions.question: What does an AR product-visualization app let a customer do before deciding to buy?
options: Watch a previous customer's review from their own real space
Measure the height and length of their own real space
See a digital product placed in their own real space
Receive a physical sample of the product in their own real space
questions.explanation: Product-visualization apps preview how a digital product would appear in the customer's real environment, such as placing furniture in a scanned room or painting walls digitally. They do not provide physical samples, measurements, or customer reviews.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of an AR virtual try-on app before purchase?
options: To measure the height and length of an object with a phone
To judge the look of a cosmetic or watch on a digital face or hand
To view an internal vein network on a patient's skin
To place furniture in a scanned image of a room
questions.explanation: Virtual try-on apps let customers test cosmetic or watch appearances on a digital face or hand before buying. Measuring objects, placing furniture, and visualizing veins belong to other AR use cases.

questions.question: How can a handheld AR device be used to help decide a vein treatment course?
options: By projecting a virtual tape measure over the patient's skin
By injecting a dye that makes the internal vein network visible
By recording a video of the patient's hand for a later review
By pointing it at the skin surface to visualize the internal vein network
questions.explanation: The device scans the vein network and, when pointed at the skin, makes the internal vein network visible so a treatment course can be decided. It is not described as using dye, video review, or a virtual tape measure.

data.text: Concrete examples show augmented reality adding digital content to real settings and to people. Customer examples cover navigation, product preview, measurement, and virtual try-on, each using the customer's real environment or appearance as the reference. Healthcare examples use the same augmentation idea for medical training, telemedicine, real-time treatment-area information, and vein visualization. The examples move from everyday consumer experience to medical practice.
points: Augmented reality navigation apps can use beacons to tell passengers their exact location and direction in large terminals.
Augmented reality product visualization apps let customers preview furniture or wall paint in a room before purchase.
An augmented reality virtual tape measure can measure object heights and lengths with a phone, without a physical tape.
Augmented reality try-on apps let customers try cosmetic looks or watch models on a digital face or hand before purchase.
Healthcare augmented reality applications include medical training, telemedicine, real-time treatment-area information, and AccuVein patient vein visualization.

questions.question: What determines the two broad categories of augmented reality systems?
options: The technology used in augmented reality systems
The number of users present in augmented reality systems
The comfort level felt in augmented reality systems
The immersion level perceived in augmented reality systems
questions.explanation: Augmented reality systems are divided by the technology used, not by psychological or immersive experience. The tempting immersion-level answer belongs to the kind of categorization used for virtual reality systems.

questions.question: Why can a marker-based augmented reality app stop working after it has been deployed outdoors?
options: A missed object recognition may prevent the app from working
A damaged marker may prevent the app from working
A failed projector may prevent the app from working
A changed GPS fix may prevent the app from working
questions.explanation: Marker-based apps depend on physical markers in the environment, and a damaged marker can make the app fail. The other options describe failures of location-based, projection-based, or recognition-based approaches.

questions.question: What do the four markerless augmented reality subcategories have in common?
options: They require a QR code to trigger the digital content
They require a GPS fix to trigger the digital content
They do not require a physical marker to trigger the digital content
They require a projector beam to trigger the digital content
questions.explanation: All markerless subcategories avoid physical markers. A QR code is a marker-based trigger, while GPS fixes and projector beams belong only to particular markerless subtypes.

questions.question: Which markerless augmented reality subtype presents digital content when the user reaches a particular location?
options: Projection-based applications
Outlining-based applications
Superimposition-based applications
Location-based applications
questions.explanation: Location-based markerless applications use a location sensor, such as GPS, to show digital content when the user is at a specific location. The other subtypes rely on object recognition, projection, or scene outlining.

questions.question: How does an outlining-based augmented reality application help a driver see nearby cars in low light?
options: It anchors a digital car at a GPS position in order to provide information for the driver
It waits for a marker on the car in order to provide an enhanced view for the driver
It projects digital cars onto the road immediately in order to provide alerts for the driver
It recreates the immediate surroundings and digitally enhances the view for the driver
questions.explanation: Outlining-based applications use object recognition to recreate the user's immediate surroundings and digitally enhance the view. Projectors, GPS anchoring, and physical markers describe other AR techniques.

data.text: Augmented reality applications divide into marker-based and markerless systems according to their technology. Marker-based systems depend on detectable markers, while markerless systems avoid physical markers and are therefore more versatile. Within markerless augmented reality, location-based, superimposition-based, projection-based, and outlining-based subtypes differ in how they detect or project digital content into the real-world view.
points: Augmented reality applications are categorized technologically as marker-based or markerless, not by psychological or immersive experience.
Marker-based augmented reality applications show content at detected markers such as QR codes, but damaged markers make them hard to maintain.
Markerless augmented reality applications are more versatile, need no physical markers, and have four recognized subtypes.
Location-based and superimposition-based markerless augmented reality applications use location sensors or computer-vision object recognition.
Projection-based and outlining-based markerless augmented reality applications use light projectors or object recognition to enhance views.

questions.question: Why are augmented reality systems commonly classified as marker-based or markerless rather than by the degree of immersion they provide?
options: Because their categories follow the psychological experience produced by the systems
Because their categories follow the display hardware worn to view the systems
Because their categories follow the realism of the content added to the systems
Because their categories follow the technology used to build and deploy the systems
questions.explanation: AR categories are based primarily on the technology used to develop and deploy the system, not on psychological immersion. VR is the side where categories follow the psychological or immersion aspect.

questions.question: What makes marker-based augmented reality systems easy to build but difficult to maintain in many real environments?
options: Their simple algorithms depend on physical markers that can be damaged
Their holographic-projection algorithms depend on physical markers that can be damaged
Their location-sensor algorithms depend on physical markers that can be damaged
Their computer-vision algorithms depend on physical markers that can be damaged
questions.explanation: Marker-based AR is easier to make because it uses simple algorithms, but the physical markers must be maintained and can be damaged, especially outside a carefully kept environment.

questions.question: How do markerless augmented reality techniques reduce the maintenance problem of marker-based augmented reality?
options: By detecting needed cues mainly with holographic projection and sometimes with sensors
By detecting needed cues mainly with computer vision and sometimes with sensors
By detecting needed cues mainly with immersive rendering and sometimes with sensors
By detecting needed cues mainly with QR-code scanning and sometimes with sensors
questions.explanation: Markerless AR avoids dependence on placed markers by relying mainly on computer vision, with other sensors such as GPS used in location-based cases.

questions.question: In the experience they provide, how do augmented reality applications mainly differ from virtual reality applications?
options: They replace the physical room with a synthetic environment in the user's real-world view
They hide the user's movement from the user's real-world view
They remove physical objects from the user's real-world view
They add digital content to the user's real-world view
questions.explanation: AR emphasizes augmenting the real-world view with digital content, whereas VR applications are characterized by immersion rather than by adding content to the physical view.

data.text: Virtual reality and augmented reality are categorized and used in contrasting ways. Virtual reality systems are grouped by how immersive the psychological experience is, while augmented reality systems are grouped mainly by the technology used, especially whether markers are required. Marker-based augmented reality is simpler but depends on markers that are hard to maintain, so markerless methods using computer vision and other techniques become important. Both technologies have overlapping application domains, but virtual reality aims to immerse the user, whereas augmented reality adds digital content to the real-world view.
points: Virtual reality system categories are based on psychological immersion: non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive.
Augmented reality system categories are based primarily on technology rather than psychology, and are marker-based or markerless.
Marker-based augmented reality is easier to make using simple algorithms, but markers need sanitized, well-attended environments.
Markerless augmented reality overcomes marker maintenance mainly with computer vision, sometimes GPS, superimposition, outline, or projection-based techniques.
Virtual reality and augmented reality share similar application domains, but virtual reality is immersive while augmented reality augments reality.

items.reason: Location-based, superimposition-based and projection-based are subcategories of markerless augmented reality, while marker-based is a broad augmented reality system category.

questions.question: Why are augmented reality system categories based mainly on implementation technology rather than on the degree of immersion, unlike virtual reality system categories?
questions.reference_answer: Virtual reality systems are categorized by psychological immersion, comprising non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive systems. Augmented reality does not require an immersive experience; it emphasizes augmenting real-world content with digital content. Therefore, AR system categories are based primarily on the technology used to develop and deploy them, broadly marker-based and markerless.

questions.question: How do markerless augmented reality techniques address the main maintenance problem of marker-based augmented reality systems?
questions.reference_answer: Marker-based augmented reality systems are easy to build but difficult to maintain because markers are prone to damage, and a damaged marker may make the application not work. Markerless augmented reality techniques overcome this difficulty by not requiring physical markers; they can use computer vision and allow users to decide where to place virtual objects. This makes them more versatile than marker-based systems.

questions.question: How does AccuVein illustrate the way augmented reality applications in healthcare support diagnosis and treatment planning?
questions.reference_answer: Healthcare augmented reality applications include medical training, telemedicine options, and real-time information that supports diagnosis, surgery, and treatment plans. AccuVein is a handheld AR device that scans a patient's vein network and, by being pointed at the skin surface, lets the internal vein network be visualized. It can indicate the patient's condition, reduce escalation by 45%, and help decide the treatment course, illustrating how AR can support clinical decision-making.

questions.question: How do augmented reality customer-experience and try-on applications in commerce contribute to the motivation for the metaverse?
questions.reference_answer: Customer-experience and try-on augmented reality applications let customers preview or try a product before purchase, for example by placing IKEA objects in a scanned room, digitally painting walls, or trying cosmetic and watch models. The presence of many such augmented reality applications in commerce, particularly e-commerce, is one motivation for the metaverse concept.
